No REQ lacks a verifiable downstream check.

Every capability stated in the Overview (requirements.md:9-19) traces 1:1 to a REQ with its own ACs: three-valued setting -> REQ-001/AC-001-004,031 (:23-45); host-independence -> REQ-002/AC-005-006 (:47-59); standing's skip+audit -> REQ-003/AC-007-010,030 (:61-85); off's persistent forbiddance -> REQ-004/AC-011-014 (:87-105); per-feature default preserved -> REQ-005/AC-015 (:107-113); Design-Source field reflection -> REQ-006/AC-016-019,029 (:115-141); live re-read -> REQ-007/AC-020-021 (:143-155); fallback-document consequence -> REQ-008/AC-022-024 (:157-175). No stated goal is left without a matching AC.

Acceptance criteria specify concrete, externally observable document-text assertions rather than vague intent, consistent with this feature's declared document-conformance style (acceptance-tests.md:3). Examples: AC-002 (requirements.md:31-33) 'Verified by asserting the section heading and the key name both exist, not by asserting the heading alone'; AC-025 (requirements.md:183-191) names five specific pre-existing rows and a before/after baseline diff rather than an unqualified 'passes' claim; AC-020 (requirements.md:149-151) is framed as an executable comparison, operationalized by TEST-044 (acceptance-tests.md:58).

Non-goals section (requirements.md:209-216) explicitly excludes: implementing #139/design-sync-scan (with the serialization caveat stated), touching plugins/sdd-lite/skills/lite-spec/SKILL.md, touching contracts/design-system.contract.v1.schema.json, adding a protected-file guard for AGENTS.md/ds_upload_consent, adding a docs/THREAT-MODEL.md entry, and re-litigating DS-29's per-feature/session/decline/withdrawal/push-failure rules. Each exclusion states the reason it is out of scope.

Baseline Constraints BL-001 through BL-006 (requirements.md:239-246) state material compatibility, data-shape, and process constraints (DS-29's gate/content unmodified; five existing field names and Egress-Consent domain unchanged; zero-upload and no-'consent'-substring invariants preserved; no protected file touched; workflow-state-registry.json entry; AGENTS.md Active Spec Directories update deferred). The security/approval boundary is explicitly disclosed rather than silently omitted: requirements.md:13-15 and :214 state plainly that AGENTS.md is unguarded and that an agent, not only a human, could write ds_upload_consent: standing, recorded as the feature's principal residual risk.

High-risk claim is explicit: requirements.md:13 states standing 'removes the one bounded moment of live human attention DS-29's entire design exists to defend' and reconstructs the exact blast radius DS-29's own security review closed as R2; requirements.md:15 states AGENTS.md carries no protected-file guard, so an agent could set the value with no distinction from deliberate human configuration. A validation surface exists on two axes: (a) acceptance criteria requiring a traceable audit record on every standing/off occasion (AC-008/AC-009/AC-016-019/AC-029, requirements.md:71-85,123-141), so the residual risk is at least detectable after the fact, and (b) a named manual-inspection target, security-spec.md, explicitly stated to carry 'the full treatment' of the risk (requirements.md:13) and recorded as the tracked residual risk (requirements.md:214). Not SKIP because a concrete high-risk claim is present with an identified surface.

No domain/ directory exists at the project root (verified via Glob on domain/*, the single permitted existence-check exception per review-context-boundary.md:154-156), so no domain/context-map.md with Domain-Model-Status: Approved and no domain/domain-contract.json exist either.
